name: Band-tailed Antshrike
rangeDescription: Suriname, french guiana, and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: A rarely encountered large antshrike. Both sexes are distinctive; male is mostly black with a broad white tail band, whereas female is mostly rusty-colored with a black face and throat.

name: Royal Penguin
rangeDescription: Macquarie island and adjacent islets
description: The largest crested penguin, with a diagnostic whitish face. Only breeds on the Australian-administered Macquarie Island; occasionally seen off of New Zealand’s subantarctic islands, rarely off of the mainland.

name: Albertine Owlet
rangeDescription: Poorly known; reported from eastern democratic republic of the congo (itombwe mountains and forest west of lake edward) and northern rwanda
description: Chunky brownish owlet. Shows bars and spots on the underparts and fine spotting on the nape and top of the head.

name: White-throated Pewee
rangeDescription: Suriname to french guiana and far northeastern brazil (amapá)
description: Small, inconspicuous, locally-distributed flycatcher. Both sexes are entirely dark gray with exception of prominent white throat patch.

name: Abyssinian Roller
rangeDescription: Senegambia to ethiopia, somalia, and kenya; central arabia
description: A slim and beautiful roller with very long outer tail feathers. In flight, the spectacular wings are half pale blue and half dark blue.

name: Spinifexbird
rangeDescription: Spinifex regions of north-central australia (pilbara to northwestern queensland)
description: A flat-crowned, plain brownish bird with a long tail found in arid spinifex/tussock grassland in inland Australia. Fairly secretive and skulking but inquisitive.

name: Three-striped Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru to northern bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Small tanager with a boldly striped head. Olive gray above, tawny orange below, with a black face and crown and a white eyebrow.

name: Red-browed Amazon
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (alagoas and bahia to rio de janeiro and são paulo)
description: Large and mostly green parrot, notable for its orange-red forehead, grading to purplish-brown on the hind-crown, a reddish base of the bill, and wing patches framed by dark purplish flight feathers. A rare and threatened inhabitant of the canopy of humid, usually lowland forests.

name: White-throated Tit
rangeDescription: Birch and pine forest of northern pakistan and northwestern india
description: A tiny bird with a small bill, a large head, and a proportionally long tail. Note the white forehead, the white throat, and the partially white collar.

name: White-crowned Parrot
rangeDescription: Caribbean slope of southeastern mexico to western panama
description: Medium-size, blue-green parrot of tropical lowlands, mainly in humid forest and forest edge. The big white crown patch and white throat on a bluish head are distinctive; also note the pinkish-red patch under the tail.

name: Sykes's Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds lower volga river eastward to eastern kazakhstan (lake balkhash) and extreme western china (western and central xinjiang), southward to southern iran, afghanistan, and western pakistan, locally in northwestern india; small resident population in northeastern united arab emirates (khor kalba) and northwestern oman (mangroves of batinah coast); non-breeding to indian subcontinent
description: Plain brown warbler with pale legs. Breeds in Central Asia; winters primarily on the Indian peninsula.

name: Orange-cheeked Honeyeater
rangeDescription: West-central new guinea (timberline zone of snow mountains)
description: A fairly large honeyeater of upper montane and subalpine forest and shrubbery. Overall olive color, light streaking with paler grayish belly and yellow legs.

name: Caribbean Martin
rangeDescription: West indies (except cuba and isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba); tobago
description: A graceful aerial feeder found over a wide variety of open habitats, especially near water, including marshes and towns. Often seen on exposed perches including power and telephone lines in villages.

name: Green-backed Tailorbird
rangeDescription: Northern and central luzon (philippines)
description: A small, long-billed, long-tailed bird of dense tangled undergrowth in lowland and foothill forest and bamboo in northern Luzon. Has olive-green wings, back, and tail, a pale gray belly, a gray chest with streaks, a rufous cap reaching below the eye, and orange legs.

name: Tawny-tufted Toucanet
rangeDescription: Far eastern colombia and southern venezuela to northwestern brazil
description: Small toucan. Look for the blue patch on a reddish bill.

name: Black-winged Lovebird
rangeDescription: Highland forest of ethiopia
description: A small, short-tailed parrot that is mostly dark green. Males have a red patch above the bill and black underwings that are distinctive in flight.

name: Whitehead's Trogon
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo
description: Breathtaking, thickset trogon found only in Borneo’s north-central mountains. Male is predominantly bright red, whereas the female is mostly tan-orange; both sexes have a broad silverish “apron”, orangish-brown back, dark face, and blue bill and skin around the eyes.

name: Fork-tailed Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro, southern minas gerais, and northeastern são paulo)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a very distinctive head pattern and tail. Best field marks are the cinnamon head and the long, forked white-tipped tail framed by a dark border.

name: Lesser Scaup
rangeDescription: Breeds north america from northern alaska and western canada southward through northern california, southern colorado, and minnesota (usa); winters to hawaiian islands, the caribbean, and northern south america
description: Peak-headed diving duck. Males have black breast, finely-barred gray back, whitish sides (often slightly dusty-looking), and yellow eye.

name: Gray-cheeked Warbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern india to southwestern china, myanmar, and indochina
description: Striking small warbler with bright white spectacles around each large dark eye; a refreshingly distinctive bird in a particularly frustrating group, thanks to its uniquely dark gray head. Active primarily in the lower levels of broadleaf forests in hilly and montane areas with dense undergrowth.
